description: Opt-in cap on the number of sampled TRAINING pairs, --max-pairs K (design.md section 16.3, Jay via orchestrator 2026-10-26). Default 0 = no cap and no new op (goldens max |diff| 0). Pair count k = min(K, max(floor, round(p N (N - 1)))) (and <= N (N - 1) as today), floor from --min-pairs (1 or N), i.e. the cap is applied after the min-pairs rule; when k == N with --min-pairs n the N-cycle sampling stays. Applies to the linear pairwise loss (--p-pair) and the deform pairwise Dice + LNCC (--p-pdice; LNCC reuses the Dice pairs); train_<task>/n_pairs stays logged. Reason: at p 0.1, k ~ 0.1 N^2 (N 32 -> 99, 48 -> 226, 64 -> 403). Also carries the script-default requirements for FEAT-005 (MAX_PAIRS=64, PAIR_RECOMPUTE=false at levels 4 and 2). Must be done BEFORE FEAT-005 (the scripts pass --max-pairs). Independent of FEAT-002..004.
steps: data_loading/postprocess.py: num_pairs(n, p_pair=0.1, min_pairs='1', max_pairs=0) and num_pairs_static(..., max_pairs=0): when max_pairs > 0 (Python int switch) return tf.minimum(k_today, max_pairs) / min(k_today, max_pairs); when 0 build exactly today's ops. sample_pairs(generator, n, p_pair, min_pairs, max_pairs=0): pass max_pairs to num_pairs; the RNG draw (one uniform([n (n - 1)])) is unchanged; with min_pairs 'n' the existing tf.cond(k == n, cycle, topk) stays (so a cap that yields k == N keeps the cycle); with min_pairs '1' and max_pairs 0 the ops are identical to today. Validate max_pairs: int >= 0 else ValueError. LinearPostprocess / DeformPostprocess: new kwarg max_pairs=0 stored and forwarded to sample_pairs.

models/memory_model.py num_pairs and tests/gpu/check_mixed_run.py expected_pairs (stdlib mirror): add the same max_pairs cap (default 0); check_mixed_run reads config.json args.max_pairs (missing -> 0) in _check_min_pairs so --expect-min-pairs n stays correct with a cap.

runtime/run.py: TrainConfig.max_pairs: int = 0, passed to both post-processes; wherever the static pair count is computed for --pair-recompute (num_pairs_static) pass max_pairs too; Trainer.__init__ re-check max_pairs is an int >= 0 (ValueError).

runtime/args.py: --max-pairs K (int, default 0) next to --min-pairs; help: 'cap on the sampled training pairs per step (linear pairwise loss and deform pairwise Dice/LNCC), applied after --min-pairs (k = min(K, max(floor, round(p N (N-1))))); 0 = no cap (default)'. parse_args: K < 0 -> parser.error; train_config_from_args passes max_pairs. If --min-pairs n and 0 < K < N, print nothing at parse time (allowed; the cap wins) but main.py logs one NOTE line 'max-pairs K < N: the min-pairs n floor is capped'. Validation pairs (--val-deform-max-pairs) are unaffected.

Record in the --pair-recompute help and the runtime/args.py module docstring: level-1 option only; it unrolls one serialized block per pair and at level 4 with N 48 (226 pairs) graph construction ran ~2 h at 99 % CPU (cluster job 10519650). Optional NOTE in main.py when --pair-recompute true at --level 4 or 2.

Tests: tests/test_postprocess.py (or the module that tests sample_pairs/num_pairs today): counts with and without the cap (tensor and static num_pairs, N in {4, 8, 32, 48, 64}, p 0.1, K in {0, 16, 64}); cap together with --min-pairs n (k = min(K, max(N, round(...))); a cap landing exactly on k == N returns a valid N-cycle: every index once as i and once as j); max_pairs 0 gives the identical pairs and generator state as before (bit-exact). memory_model.num_pairs and check_mixed_run.expected_pairs agree with postprocess for the same grid. tests/test_main.py (or the args test module): --max-pairs -1 and --max-pairs 1.5 -> SystemExit; default 0; --max-pairs 64 reaches TrainConfig.max_pairs. tests/test_check_mixed_run.py: _check_min_pairs with args.max_pairs set. Goldens unmodified.

tests/gpu/measure_level_memory.py: accept --max-pairs K as a comma list like the other knobs (default '0'); each measured config records max_pairs and the resulting n_pairs (per task, from the same num_pairs rule) in the JSON output; part of the config cross product / one config per process as today.

slurm/m10_batch_memory_capped.sh (new, modelled on slurm/m10_batch_memory.sh, commit aa0855f): #SBATCH -A qtim (never entre) -p rtx8000 --gpus=1 -N 1 --ntasks-per-node=1 --cpus-per-task=3 --mem=64G, logs under /autofs/space/crater_001/users/jn85/BrainRegProjects/GroupwiseReg/logs, same container/binds, --isolate true, a timeout per step, output scratch/m10/memory_batch_capped.json. All configs with --max-pairs 64: level 4 deform N 48, 64, 80, 96 (--gradient-checkpointing full, --lean-sampler true, --split-group-conv true, NO --pair-recompute, LNCC 1/1, --min-pairs n, validation pass with --val-pair-chunk 16); level 4 linear N 128, 160, 192 preceded by an int32 element check (stem tensor N x 40 x 56 x 48 x 32 must be < 2^31 elements; skip + record the N that exceed it); level 2 deform N 16 (compare with the uncapped 29.9 GB at 24 pairs); level 2 linear N 32, 40. Header: what it measures, the uncapped reference facts of design 16.5, 'DO NOT submit without Jay's approval; at most two active jobs'. The orchestrator submits it after the workflow; add it to tests/run_tests_wsl.sh's bash -n list and, if cheap, a static header check (qtim, rtx8000, --max-pairs 64, no --pair-recompute) in tests/test_slurm_scripts.py.

FEAT-005 requirement (scripts; implement there, listed here so it is not lost): slurm/r_level4.sh, r_level2.sh, r_level1.sh default MAX_PAIRS=64 (validated integer >= 0, exit 2 otherwise) -> --max-pairs $MAX_PAIRS on the main.py line (common flag); PAIR_RECOMPUTE default false in r_level4.sh and r_level2.sh (true stays in r_level1.sh); header note on why (job 10519650). The dry-run expectations of design 11.5 h change accordingly: r_level4 default / r_level2 contain --pair-recompute false, r_level1 --pair-recompute true, all three --max-pairs 64.
